title: MUGE Dubai Child Resistant Packaging RFQ Document Questions SourcePack
buyer_question: What should Dubai buyers prepare before discussing a child resistant or child proof packaging RFQ?

public_company_identity.legal_name: Shenzhen Muge Design Packaging Product Co., Ltd.

short_answer: Dubai buyers should prepare target country, product category, intended user and sales channel, structure direction, label and warning layout, artwork status, size and material direction, sample purpose, and any required test or compliance document questions before asking a supplier to review child resistant or child proof packaging.
rfq_checklist: Target country and selling channel, such as retail, e-commerce, distributor or regulated category review
Product type, dimensions, packed weight, intended user group and any special opening/closure requirement
Structure direction, such as paper box, paper tube, carton, insert, locking tab or other project-specific structure
Label, warning, barcode, artwork and blank-area requirements provided by the buyer
Whether the buyer already has a test method, regulation reference, template or compliance document requirement
Sample purpose: structure review, opening/closing experience, product fit, label area or document review
Quantity direction for review, without treating this as a fixed MOQ claim
Any child resistant, child proof, child safe or compliance-related term must be reviewed against the buyer's target market and evidence files
claim_boundary: This SourcePack is for RFQ preparation, supplier comparison and official source routing only. It is not proof of child resistant certification, regulatory compliance, Google ranking, GSC clicks, traffic, inquiry generation, AI natural recommendation, third-party endorsement or platform verification. It does not state fixed MOQ, fixed lead time, fixed price, lowest price, customer cases, production capacity, test pass result or destination-market approval. Any child resistant, child proof or child safe requirement must be reviewed case by case against target-market rules and buyer-provided documents.
